description: A seven-channel step sequencer whose steps are recorded rather than programmed: with record on the knobs and inputs are written into the current stage, and stepping plays those values back

params.text: Moves the sequence to any stage, its travel divided across the whole sequence length
Sets how many stages the sequence holds, 0 to 128
Advances the sequence by one stage on each press, wrapping round at the end
Steps the sequence back by one stage on each press, wrapping round at the start
Returns the sequence to the first stage on each press
Steps that channel through three modes on each press: the value passed straight out, the value snapped to semitones, and a 10V trigger fired when the stage changes
Sets that channel's value for the current stage, -10V to 10V; while record is off the knob shows the stored value for the stage the sequence is on
Starts writing the knobs and inputs into the stages on each press and stops on the next; its lamp is red while recording and blue while recording in edit mode

inputs.text: A rise returns the sequence to the first stage
A rise advances the sequence by one stage
A rise steps the sequence back by one stage
A rise starts and stops recording
The value written into that channel of the current stage while record is on, in place of that channel's knob; with nothing patched the channel takes the next channel of the cable above it

outputs.text: That channel's stored value for the current stage, passed straight out, snapped to semitones, or as a 10V trigger, depending on that channel's mode button

notes: nothing is stored until record is on: with record off the module plays back what is already in its stages and ignores the input jacks
shift-clicking a channel knob writes that value into every stage of the sequence at once
menu: Set Max Sequence Length — a submenu of lengths setting the ceiling the MAX STAGES knob is measured against, up to 2048 stages
Stop Record At End — stops recording when the sequence reaches its last stage, instead of wrapping round and writing over what is already there
Edit Mode — records only the channel whose knob is being turned, leaving the other six stages' values alone
Set Polyphony for Channel 1 — a submenu from 1 to 7 channels gathering that many channels' outputs into the first output as polyphonic channels
